purpose: Miconazole nitrate is used to treat fungal infections like vaginal yeast infections, athlete's foot, jock itch, and ringworm. It can also help with fungal skin rashes. It works on the skin or inside the vagina depending on the form you use.
how_it_works: Miconazole works by attacking the outer layer of the fungus, called its cell membrane. It pokes holes in that membrane, causing the fungus to leak and die. Basically, it stops the fungus from growing and spreading so your body can heal.
common_side_effects: When used on the skin, you might notice mild burning, stinging, redness, or irritation where you apply it. For vaginal products, some women feel mild burning or itching inside. These effects are usually mild and go away as you continue treatment.
warnings: Do not use this medicine in or near your eyes. If your symptoms do not improve after a week or two, check with your doctor — you may have a different type of infection. Talk to your doctor before using vaginal miconazole if you have never been diagnosed with a yeast infection before, if you are pregnant, or if you have a fever or other unusual symptoms. Some forms may weaken condoms or diaphragms, so check the label.
typical_dosing: For skin infections like athlete's foot or ringworm, apply a thin layer to the affected area twice a day for 2 to 4 weeks. For vaginal yeast infections, Monistat comes in 1-day, 3-day, or 7-day treatment options depending on the strength — follow the package directions carefully. Always finish the full course of treatment even if you feel better sooner.
